raw_case_text:
A 72-year-old male farmer with no prior medical history presented to our emergency room with fever and bilateral calf pain for 3 days, followed by hemoptysis for 1 day. Upon arrival at the emergency room, the patient experienced respiratory distress and orthopnea, with a body temperature of 38.6 C, respiratory rate of 30 breaths/min, pulse rate of 129 beats/min, and blood pressure of 129/70 mmHg. With an oxygen mask at 8 L/min, the oxygen saturation was 89%. Chest CT revealed bilateral pulmonary exudative changes (Figure 2A). His initial lab results were: P/F, 124 mmHg; PLT, 12 x 109/L; CRP, 219.72 mg/L; PCT, 74.68 ng/mL; APTT, 30 s; MYO, >2000 ng/mL; CR, 128 mg/dL; ALT, 98 U/L; TBIL, 64.1 mumol/L. The primary diagnosis included severe pneumonia, DAH, severe ARDS, and hepatic and renal dysfunction.
The patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated with 100% FiO2 support, but his P/F declined to 66 mmHg. Emergency VV-ECMO and CRRT support were initiated, along with intermittent prone ventilation. He remained on volume-controlled ventilation (tidal volume 200-300 mL, PEEP 20 cmH2O, plateau pressure <=35 mmHg). Empirical antibiotic therapy included moxifloxacin (0.4 g IV daily) combined with imipenem/cilastatin (1 g IV every 8 h). The patient also received methylprednisolone (500 mg IV for 3 days), recombinant human thrombopoietin (15,000 U SC daily), fresh plasma, packed red blood cells, norepinephrine (0.1-1.2 mug/kg/min), and bronchoscopic alveolar lavage. Both blood and lavage fluid were sent for mNGS testing. On day 3, mNGS confirmed leptospirosis, and platelet transfusion (10 U) was administered on day 4, but a follow-up chest CT showed worsening pulmonary hemorrhage (Figure 2B). On day 11, VV-ECMO was discontinued, and a follow-up chest CT showed significant improvement in pulmonary hemorrhage (Figure 2C). The total duration of VV-ECMO support was 255 h, with the first 60 h without UFH anticoagulation. On day 15, the endotracheal tube was removed. On day 17, the patient was transferred out of the EICU. On day 21, the patient was discharged after recovery. A follow-up chest CT before discharge showed that pulmonary hemorrhage had significantly improved (Figure 2D). The treatment process is summarized in Figure 2E, and the trends in blood test results are detailed in Table 3. Changes in ventilator parameters, ECMO parameters, and medication dosages during ECMO are detailed in Table 2.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 72-year-old male farmer presented with fever and bilateral calf pain for 3 days, followed by hemoptysis and respiratory distress for 1 day.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented to the emergency department after 3 days of fever and bilateral calf myalgia that progressed to frank hemoptysis, acute respiratory distress, and orthopnea 1 day prior to arrival.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy farmer with no prior medical history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, bilateral calf pain, hemoptysis, dyspnea, and orthopnea.

objective.physical_examination: Emergency department vital signs: temperature 38.6 °C, respiratory rate 30 breaths/min, pulse 129 beats/min, blood pressure 129/70 mmHg, and SpO2 89% on 8 L/min oxygen mask, with visible respiratory distress and orthopnea.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial labs: PaO2/FiO2 ratio 124 mmHg (dropping to 66 mmHg after intubation on 100% FiO2), platelets 12 × 10⁹/L, CRP 219.72 mg/L, procalcitonin 74.68 ng/mL, aPTT 30 s, myoglobin >2,000 ng/mL, creatinine 128 µmol/L (reported as 128 mg/dL in text), ALT 98 U/L, and total bilirubin 64.1 µmol/L.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission chest CT demonstrated bilateral pulmonary exudative changes. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) and blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) confirmed Leptospira infection on hospital day 3. Repeat chest CT on day 4 showed transiently worsened pulmonary hemorrhage, followed by marked resolution on day 11 and pre-discharge CT scans.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed severe pulmonary hemorrhagic leptospirosis presenting with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH), severe ARDS, severe thrombocytopenia, and hepatorenal dysfunction, confirmed by blood and BALF mNGS on day 3. Treated with emergency endotracheal intubation, VV-ECMO (255 hours total; heparin-free for the first 60 hours), continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), intermittent prone ventilation, IV moxifloxacin (0.4 g daily) plus imipenem-cilastatin (1 g q8h), IV methylprednisolone (500 mg daily for 3 days), subcutaneous recombinant human thrombopoietin (15,000 U daily), platelet (10 U), FFP, and PRBC transfusions, and norepinephrine (0.1–1.2 µg/kg/min). VV-ECMO was successfully weaned on day 11, the patient was extubated on day 15, transferred from the EICU on day 17, and discharged recovered on day 21.
